arxiv-1507-03840.title: Using interrogative logic to teach classical logic This work is part of the project on the interrogative model of inquiry and education currently under development at Yachay Tech.
arxiv-1507-03840.creator: Levis Zerpa
arxiv-1507-03840.description: Abstract In the paper I discuss a tool for helping students in their symbolizations of natural language sentences using the formal language of classical first order logic (CFOL). The tool is an extension of Hintikka’s concept of (Inquirer’s) range of attention in the context of interrogative games.

arxiv-2209-14426.creator: Jacqueline Ankenbauer, Kaveh Fathian, Jonathan P. How
arxiv-2209-14426.description: Abstract This paper proposes a novel framework for real-time localization and egomotion tracking of a vehicle in a reference map. The core idea is to map the semantic objects observed by the vehicle and register them to their corresponding objects in the reference map.

arxiv-2211-03973.title: The Wentaculus: Density Matrix Realism Meets the Arrow of Time
arxiv-2211-03973.creator: Eddy Keming Chen
arxiv-2211-03973.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Eddy Keming Chen. 1

Introduction

Two of the most difficult problems in the foundations of physics are (1) what gives rise to the arrow of time and (2) what the ontology of quantum mechanics is. They are difficult because the fundamental dynamical laws of physics do not privilege an arrow of time, and the quantum-mechanical wave function describes a high-dimensional reality that is radically different from our ordinary experiences.

pmc-11470512.description: The ST6GAL1 sialyltransferase is overexpressed in multiple cancers, including pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). pmc-12702339.creator: Ravi Shankar Goutam, Neha Kaushik, Basant Kumar, Woochan Jung, Santosh Kumar, Seung-Hwan Lee, Unjoo Lee, Jaebong Kim
pmc-12702339.description: The Iroquois (Iro/Irx) gene family encodes transcription factors that belong to the Three-Amino-Acid Loop Extension-class homeodomain group, distinguished by a conserved Iro-box domain. Iroquois signaling is evolutionarily conserved from invertebrates to vertebrates and plays a vital role in embryonic development. In invertebrates, Iro/Irx genes control tissue compartmentalization, whereas in vertebrates, they regulate gastrulation, neural patterning, and organogenesis.
